item.title: Education is foundation for Hela’s future
item.description: Education is the foundation for the future of Hela Province, says Governor Philip Undialu. “Every student who graduates represents another opportunity for our province to build a better, more skilled and responsible generation. Because of this significant event, we had to postpone the Pori LLG Gun Surrender Program scheduled for Thursday to today, Friday,” he said.
item.content:encoded:
Education is the foundation for the future of Hela Province, says Governor Philip Undialu.

“Every student who graduates represents another opportunity for our province to build a better, more skilled and responsible generation. Because of this significant event, we had to postpone the Pori LLG Gun Surrender Program scheduled for Thursday to today, Friday,” he said.

Speaking during the Hoiebia Secondary School graduation last Thursday in Tebi LLG, Tari-Pori District, Governor Undialu congratulated the graduands and said their journey does not end at graduation but marks the beginning of a new chapter and greater responsibility.

A total of 60 Grade 12 students and 102 Grade 10 students graduated.

He said Hela is a new province that has faced many challenges in law and order and school infrastructure, but he acknowledged the graduands for persevering and closing one chapter of their education.

“Many students who were supposed to be inside the classroom were deprived of their rights, and as a responsible Government, we are doing all we can to address this issue. One of it is through the Illegal Gun Surrender Program, which started in this LLG first,” he said.

Governor Undialu said that the province is now in the hands of the new generation, and that is the reason he and his team have had sleepless nights to ensure guns are removed so children can focus on their education.

“Under my leadership and when the now Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu was the Education Services Director, we created 16 new high schools and upgraded 5 to secondary schools. We also created 19 FODE and TVET centres and 40 primary schools around the province so that opportunities can be made available there,” he said.

He acknowledged the Tebi LLG community for surrendering 18 high-powered guns in the name of peace, education and other Government services.

The event also coincided with the official opening of the new Administration Building and staff houses, jointly delivered through the partnership between the Hela Provincial Government and the Tari-Pori District Development Authority (DDA).

item.title: Boat and engine retrieved-11-still missing
item.description: Search and rescue teams have recovered the missing boat and its engine at Wei Island near Wewak, but the 11 passengers remain missing. The 23‑foot boat, powered by a 60hp outboard motor, left Kubugam for Dumad, South Karkar Island on Saturday night, September 26. Between 7 and 8 p.m., the vessel encountered engine failure in rough seas, began taking in water, and drifted away under strong currents
item.content:encoded:
Search and rescue teams have recovered the missing boat and its engine at Wei Island near Wewak, but the 11 passengers remain missing.

The 23‑foot boat, powered by a 60hp outboard motor, left Kubugam for Dumad, South Karkar Island on Saturday night, September 26. Between 7 and 8 p.m., the vessel encountered engine failure in rough seas, began taking in water, and drifted away under strong currents.

SAR teams reclaimed the boat and engine at Wei Island and have now retreated back to Madang for further coordination. No survivors were found with the vessel.

Team leader Udil Lapiu has appealed to Wewak islanders and coastal villages to remain vigilant and report any sightings of survivors, debris, or drift bodies. He also thanked the Karkar community in Wewak for their support in assisting the ongoing search.

Authorities emphasize that community vigilance is critical as the fate of the passengers remains unknown.

The situation remains urgent. While the boat and engine have been found, the 11 passengers are still missing. Search and rescue operations continue.

item.title: Wewak’s new school graduates first batch of grade 10 students
item.description: 75 grade 10 students of a newly established, Mambe High School school in Wewak District graduated as pioneers last Friday marking an historic occasion for Turubu LLG. Mambe High School is the second High School in Turubu that serves the rural communities of an emerging economic and agricultural hub of Est Sepik Province.
item.content:encoded:
75 grade 10 students of a newly established, Mambe High School school in Wewak District graduated as pioneers last Friday marking an historic occasion for Turubu LLG.

Mambe High School is the second High School in Turubu that serves the rural communities of an emerging economic and agricultural hub of Est Sepik Province.

Despite critical development milestones, parents and teachers have managed to conclude the academic year for their first grade 10 students.

"This is the history I have been telling you about", says Gregory Naro.

Naro is the BOG Chairman who pushed for the establishment of the school in 2025. School Head Teacher Lux Mailen says parental contributions have brought the new school and it's growing needs to the end.

This successful 1st grade 10 graduation reflects strong parental support and excellent working relationship between students, parents and teachers. It also reflects the the commitment of rural people to sustaining basic services.

Local MP Stanley Samban who has contributed to the school's development urged the people of Turubu to look after basic services and appoint leaders who will bring services into their local communities. Noting his precious support to Turubu LLG, Samban expressed his commitment to continue that strong support in delivering critical development milestones.

The 75 pioneer students from Mambe High School are now sitting for their first National Exams, joining 63 students from their neighbor Mandi High School.

item.title: Prime Minister Marape leaves for Tuvalu
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape is leaving the country today to join Pacific Leaders in Tuvalu to attend the special pre-COP31 Leaders’s event and hold a bilateral meeting with Tuvalu Prime Minister, Feleti Teo. The COP31 event happening in Tuvalu from October 5-8 is one that is being delivered by Fiji, Tuvalu and Australia ahead of the official COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, in November.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape is leaving the country today to join Pacific Leaders in Tuvalu to attend the special pre-COP31 Leaders’s event and hold a bilateral meeting with Tuvalu Prime Minister, Feleti Teo.

The COP31 event happening in Tuvalu from October 5-8 is one that is being delivered by Fiji, Tuvalu and Australia ahead of the official COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, in November.

According to Marape, his visit would show PNGs solidarity with Tuvalu and other small island developing states facing the serious impacts of climate change and rising sea levels.

Marape said Tuvalu is one of the smallest countries in the world in terms of population and land areas yet is on the frontline of a global climate crisis that it has contributed very little towards.

He said PNG had consistently supported solutions that would allow Tuvaluans to remain in their homeland rather than being forced to relocate due to rising sea levels.

He added that during the Pacific Islands forum Leaders Meeting in Funafuti in 2019, he advocated for the use of land reclamation, engineering and technology to help protect Tuvalu’s territory and enable its people to remain in their country.

Marape also stated that PNG has committed a total of K5 million to assist Tuvalu with land reclamation and that his meeting with Prime Minister Teo would provide an opportunity to discuss progressing this assistance.

Furthermore, Marape said the situation in Tuvalu should also send a strong message to major economies and major greenhouse-gas emitters.

He also thanked Australia for its leadership in ensuring Pacific priorities are elevated in the COP31 process.

item.title: Malala’s Numuru bridge reconstruction
item.description: Reconstruction work on the severed Numuru Bridge in Malala on the Madang/ Bogia Highway will take at least five days to complete. Works Manager in Madang, Job Kull said a new bailey bridge has been brought in from Lae and will be moved to site to be assembled and launched.
item.content:encoded:
Reconstruction work on the severed Numuru Bridge in Malala on the Madang/ Bogia Highway will take at least five days to complete.

Works Manager in Madang, Job Kull said a new bailey bridge has been brought in from Lae and will be moved to site to be assembled and launched.

The old bridge has been cleared and demolished.

The 32-meter single lane bailey bridge collapsed last Friday morning under an overloaded tipper truck that was heading towards Bogia with gravel for road maintenance.

On Thursday, Secretary for the Department of Works and Highways, Gibson Holemba, and Deputy Secretary Simon Suwagu visited Numuru to see the progress of work.

Mr Holemba also appealed to the local people to respect workmen who are on site.

Governor Pariwa accompanied Secretary Holemba to Numuru to get views from local villagers regarding an access road for vehicles to use following the collapsed of the bridge.

The local people are worried about their food gardens and cash crops, hence; have not made any decision yet on whether to allow the bypass to be constructed or not.

They have also stopped any passage of vehicles, even through the beach front, which was previously allowed.

All vehicle movements between Madang and Bogia have been temporarily halted.

Mr Kull said the new bridge should be installed before next weekend if there are no further delays.

item.title: Father and son legacy in police
item.description: It was a proud day at the Bomana National Center of Excellence as 55 cadet officers were commissioned as Inspectors of the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary last Friday. Among them, Inspector Andy Doa from Tambul Nebilyer District of Western Highlands Province shared an emotional salute with his father, Senior Constable Timothy Doa — pledging together their commitment to serve the nation.
item.content:encoded:
It was a proud day at the Bomana National Center of Excellence as 55 cadet officers were commissioned as Inspectors of the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary last Friday.

Among them, Inspector Andy Doa from Tambul Nebilyer District of Western Highlands Province shared an emotional salute with his father, Senior Constable Timothy Doa — pledging together their commitment to serve the nation.

The ceremony marked not only the Constabulary’s future leadership, but also the enduring legacy of service carried across generations.

The newly commissioned Inspector, Andy Doa was formerly the Branch Manager for Paradise Breweries in Goroka and joined the Constabulary’s Cadet Program in 2023.

He said his main reason for joining the cadet was to be an agent of change at a time when public confidence in police conduct is under scrutiny.

“The RPNGC’s reputation has been tarnished over the years, and I made a personal choice to improve how the Constabulary is seen by the public and to faithfully serve the country,” he said.

Doa admits the transition was challenging, moving from a management role where he was used to giving orders, to a disciplined environment that demanded listening, following instructions, and adapting to new leadership skills.

For him, the decision is both personal and symbolic: carrying his father’s legacy while striving to restore pride in the Constabulary.

Meanwhile in a moving moment after the ceremony, Senior Constable Timothy Doa, a veteran of 38 years with the Special Services Division received his son with a proud salute as he rose to the rank of Inspector.

He explained that Andy becomes the first child of SSD officers at McGregor Barracks to be granted the Inspector rank, a breakthrough that made him “the proudest man” among his comrades.

“He’s my second born son and the first child of SSD officers to pass out with the rank of Inspector. I am so proud of him,” he said.

Inspector Andy Doa has been posted to public safety in Southern Highlands Province, where he looks forward to the tasks ahead of him.

item.title: El Nino crisis: Water and food shortage hits Dom Kagul in SSY
item.description: Communities in the mountain villages of Dom Kagul, Kamtai District in Sinasina-Yongomugl are facing severe water shortage and famine as the El Nino dry spell continues to worsen. A local community leader, Dom David Kua from Dom Kagul village, said after a prolonged dry season, villages that once had abundant food and coffee along the Wahgi River are now struggling to survive.
item.content:encoded:
Communities in the mountain villages of Dom Kagul, Kamtai District in Sinasina-Yongomugl are facing severe water shortage and famine as the El Nino dry spell continues to worsen.

A local community leader, Dom David Kua from Dom Kagul village, said after a prolonged dry season, villages that once had abundant food and coffee along the Wahgi River are now struggling to survive.

He said villages on both sides of the Wahgi River bordering Gumine and Sinasina-Yongomugl Districts including Konoma, Dom Kagul, Gunangi and towards Ubanidiawa are experiencing the same situation.

"On the mountaintops, all our water holes and creeks have dried up. Even the Wahgi River is drying up. We have no water to drink and our people are starving," Kua said.

Kua added that a number of people are now suffering from diarrhea and influenza due to prolonged lack of clean drinking water and poor sanitation and hygiene.

He is now appealing to the Member for Sinasina-Yongomugl, Hon. Kerenga Kua and the District Development Authority to assist immediately.

Kua noted that the Marape-Rosso National Government had allocated K300 million nationwide for El Nino relief in the recent Supplementary Budget, and said the people of SSY are waiting urgently for relief assistance.

Efforts to get comments from the SSY DDA and Provincial Disaster Office are continuing.

item.title: Milne Bay PEC assists schools to complete academic year amid El Nino
item.description: ‎The Milne Bay Provincial Government has come to the aid of schools in Milne Bay province affected by the onset of the El Nino'. ‎They've allocated K1.2mil this week to assist schools to complete the 2026 academic year, particularly boarding schools and students preparing to sit for the upcoming National Examinations. ‎ ‎The Milne Bay Provincial Executive Council (PEC) met on Thursday evening to d
item.content:encoded: ‎The Milne Bay Provincial Government has come to the aid of schools in Milne Bay province affected by the onset of the El Nino'. ‎They've allocated K1.2mil this week to assist schools to complete the 2026 academic year, particularly boarding schools and students preparing to sit for the upcoming National Examinations. ‎ ‎The Milne Bay Provincial Executive Council (PEC) met on Thursday evening to discuss assistance for schools affected by the El Nino' conditions following a policy submission from the Provincial Division of Education. ‎ ‎Milne Bay Deputy Governor, Mathew Magioudi, told NBC News yesterday that a submission was presented to the Provincial Government for assistance, especially with the National Examinations coming up for the grades 10s and 12s. ‎ ‎"The cabinet saw that it's very important for schools to complete their 2026 academic year, mainly the grades 10s and 12s in boarding schools. The cabinet in it's wisdom endorsed a total of K1.2mil for the rescue of all the schools affected by the El Nino". Magiodu said. ‎ ‎He said because of the urgency and difficulties associated with normal procurement processes, affected schools and boarding institutions have been asked to submit their quotations and requirements for assistance. ‎ ‎ ‎Magiodi said the payment will be made to suppliers based on the submitted requirements to allow schools to access the assistance. ‎

item.title: Ume is new BX-9 interim Welterweight champion
item.description: PNG boxer John Ume, aka the Ring Monster, is now the BX-9 interim Welterweight champion after defeating Hamzy Perwaisy last night in Auckland by technical knockout in the seventh round.
